regions.region: full-page title, abstract, introduction, and lower-right Scheme 1
regions.finding: Abstract/introduction state the reaction concept; Scheme 1 is a generic R-group transformation and proposed imine/enamine route, not an individual batch experiment.

unresolved: Generic R-group structures in Scheme 1 cannot be expanded into complete individual molecules.

regions.region: upper half, Table 1 and reaction drawing
regions.finding: Eleven amine-loading/Bronsted-acid optimization rows were read row by row; entry 5 includes the MgSO4 footnote and entry 8 preserves the acid-column dash without converting it to zero.
Six solvent rows were inspected; MeNO2 at reflux gives a complicated mixture, while the five numeric outcomes are isolated yields.
Narrative corroborates the Table 1 quantities, acid comparison, MgSO4 trial, and the choice of toluene; the common 72% row is not duplicated across tables.

unresolved: Most optimization rows omit exact scale, solvent volume, atmosphere, workup, and purification.

regions.finding: Seven amine-scope rows were inspected; entry 7 has both 4ag (42%) and footnoted 5a (34%), and the text flags post-chromatography decomposition of 4ab.

regions.region: middle and lower portion, three arrows in Scheme 2
regions.finding: Three distinct substrate batches 1b, 1c, and 1d were extracted with their individual amine/PhI ratios, times, yields, and depicted products 6a--6c.
Text provides qualitative context for amine scope; it does not add a new batch beyond Table 3 and Scheme 2.

unresolved: The 34% secondary-product 5a outcome has no separately stated measurement basis; many complex structures remain machine-unverified.

regions.region: upper-left Figure 1 and adjacent Scheme 2 discussion
regions.finding: NOE drawing and prose support the relative trans assignment of 6b and the highly diastereoselective 1c/1d reactions; Figure 1 is characterization evidence, not a new experiment.
The S-2h reaction gives 6d in 69% yield with dr 1.3:1; substrate 1e gives a complicated unidentified mixture and no assigned product.

regions.region: lower half, Table 4 and reaction drawing
regions.finding: All twelve organic-iodide rows were read independently; the common PhI/4aa row is linked to the standard record and the other eleven rows remain separate scope experiments.

unresolved: Table 4 omits organic-iodide equivalents and most operational details; vinyl-iodide and complex product structures need chemical review.

regions.finding: Oxidation of 4ae to 8 (64%) and subsequent debenzylation of 8 to 9 (81%) were retained as two successive experiments, not one merged transformation.
Three control experiments were extracted: early stopping gives 4aa and enamine 7aa; 5a converts to 4aa; 1f gives no product with 83% starting material recovered.
Prose identifies 7aa as an intermediate and discusses a proposed mechanism; mechanistic interpretation is classified separately from reported batches.

unresolved: Schemes 4 and 5 omit scales, most reagent amounts, workups, and purification details; the recovery basis for 1f is unstated.

regions.finding: The R-group catalytic cycle is explicitly proposed and was stored as one mechanism record, not as experimental arrows with yields.

regions.region: left column, Experimental Section Typical Procedure
regions.finding: Exact charges, argon atmosphere, temperature/time, TLC, evaporation, chromatography, product mass, and 72% yield for 4aa were merged into the standard record repeated in Tables 1--4.

regions.region: right column references and lower-left characterization
regions.finding: Spectroscopic characterization and cited prior literature were inspected but not converted into duplicate reaction experiments.

unresolved: Supporting Information is mentioned in the paper but no SI was supplied or explicitly associated.
